Question: Address-bar fallback (no Document has a portal URL): which Documents are read?
Choice: Only on-screen Documents that give no URL of their own; a Document whose own URL is off the portals is never read
Why: WP3 text said every on-screen Document; that would read an Edge sidebar or extension pane whenever the main page exposes no URL. Same coverage for browsers without a Document URL, no privacy leak.

Question: R9: how is a page known to be heavy, and how are worker threads made?
Choice: Last read ms per lane per ctx.url (50 kept); unknown pages are not held. Each worker is a one-thread daemon executor, not ThreadPoolExecutor
Why: R9 says the last read of that page; a URL key needs no new field. ThreadPoolExecutor threads are joined at exit, so a wedged UIA call would hold the app open; daemon threads satisfy 'close() leaves wedged threads daemon'.

Question: R7 vs the WP3 move of extract_browser_url into vsdc_uia_text
Choice: address_bar_here holds the code; VSDCRouter.extract_browser_url stays and delegates to it with its own _uia and _cached_address_elements
Why: One copy so the two readers cannot drift; the crosshair path keeps its method, object and cache exactly as R7 requires (its tests unchanged and green).

Question: WP4 text says delete the router's own URL read and remove burst ticks; what was done?
Choice: Router keeps _init_uia, extract_browser_url, _cached_address_elements and its 15 ms burst ticks for the crosshair engines only; while SGT is on the worker skips burst ticks and the capture loop bursts its own reads (BURST_READS=3, 0.3 s apart)
Why: R7 overrides the deletion; burst ticks only served the crosshair OCR engine, and with SGT on a 15 ms tick would add screenshots, not reads

Question: Frame tick and the OCR flash trigger in WP4
Choice: FRAME_TICK_SEC=0.35 (worker default), FRAME_TICK_FAST_SEC=0.2 named; OCR flash read not wired (WP7), the loop keeps screenshotting during a heavy read so WP7 can fire it
Why: R10: 0.2 s only after WP0's gate probe measures a tick under 15 ms; WP7 owns the flash trigger and FLASH_MIN_CELLS

Question: How does the loop keep the URL fresh (R2) and hand reads to today's SGT?
Choice: A URL-only read is asked once the window's URL is 1 s old (SCOPE_POLL_SEC < URL_FRESH_SEC 2 s); a page read is handed to SgtShadow.observe(read={lines,docs,ms}) under the read's own URL, tab and title (_absorb_compat, deleted by WP5); torn and error results are never absorbed (R1)
Why: polling at half the freshness limit keeps the scope gate open without a gap; observe(read=) reuses the whole existing SGT path with no second read

Question: R1 closed ring and cuts: which boundaries cut a session's unanswered reads?
Choice: Ends by logout, login page, shutdown/switched off/recovered cut them; idle and window closed do not. Another client's PAN/GSTIN cuts only when it is not a new tab's first page (that is a tab switch, the reads asked on the old tab are about the old client).
Why: R1 names logout, login page and identity contradiction; a new tab's first read showing another client is the existing 'first_read' tab-switch path, not a contradiction inside one tab, and cutting it would lose the shelved session's own late reads (6.1 edge case).

Question: R6 in the dataset in progress: may OCR fill the status piece or complete the draft into a row?
Choice: No. OCR fills only empty non-status pieces and never turns the draft into a row or closes it (no new period from OCR); the next UIA read or the session end writes it. OCR rows come only from a dataset that carries its own ARN.
Why: A status piece or a draft row from OCR would let wording promote without an identifier, which R6 forbids; filling form/period/year pieces stays allowed by 5.2.

Question: absorb() details the blueprint leaves open (clock, blind counter, logout page)
Choice: absorb(result, frame, ocr, now, blind_retries): age checked on the reader's clock (now) from asked_at as the reader does; s.last_read set on SGT's own clock at absorb; the blind-retry counter lives in the loop's WindowState and is reset by a URL change or a non-blind read; observe_window returns None on a logout page and the loop asks no page read there; when a page read is the newest word on the window's URL the loop calls observe_window with it before absorb.
Why: The result's times are time.monotonic while SGT's clock is wall time; mixing them would break observe()'s 15 s re-read gate. Calling observe_window first makes a logout/login reached during the read end the session before its text could land (R1).

Question: An OCR picture has no tab bracketing like a UIA read; how is it attributed?
Choice: Held until the first clean read that began after the picture shows the same tab (absorbed), else dropped
Why: The loop's tab knowledge is up to 1 s old; a flash right after a tab switch was attributed to the old tab's session (test_b1). An immediate scope read confirms the tab.

Question: How does a toast that appears in the same tick as a navigation get a flash scan?
Choice: A change of FLASH_MIN_CELLS or more arms the flash for OCR_ARM_SEC (1 s); the first tick where UIA is busy fires it
Why: That tick's read is only just asked, so the busy test fails there; the toast is still up a tick later (R2 toast, C1 heavy).

Question: What counts as a covered background window?
Choice: Its rectangle (DWM frame bounds) is fully hidden by the union of shown windows above it in z-order (rect subtraction, 2 px slack); click-through and tool windows hide nothing; minimised, cloaked (other virtual desktop), hung and off-monitor windows are never watched behind
Why: 4.7 only named the foreground's rectangle; a browser behind two side-by-side programs, or behind a maximised program that is not in front, is just as covered (Chromium builds no tree) and would read blind and raise false health alerts; IsHungAppWindow keeps PrintWindow off a hung browser

Question: Which background windows get the MAX_WATCHED_WINDOWS slots?
Choice: Window in front first, then background windows titled like a portal (router PORTAL_KEYWORDS), then the rest by z-order
Why: with more than 2 visible browser windows a news or PiP window must not take a lane slot from a portal window; uses the router's existing quick gate, no new portal rule

Question: How do background windows feed health and the unlisted-portal tripwire?
Choice: Health counts a background window in scope only on a fresh Document URL, never raises scope-lost for it, and each absorbed read names its window (HealthMonitor.reading); the tripwire looks only at the window in front; heartbeat front/page fields stay the front window's, plus bg=<count>
Why: WP10 rule: blind only if its Document URL is in scope and not covered; read_result had no window and would land on whichever window was looked at last; the tripwire probes UI names of an unlisted page, so its reach is not widened
